title: Split Seconds
statement: Ek function `split_time(total_seconds)` likho jo seconds ki ek non-negative integer value le aur ek tuple `(hours, minutes, seconds)` return kare. Example: `split_time(3661)` ka answer `(1, 1, 1)` hai.
hint: Ek ghante mein 3600 seconds hote hain; `//` aur `%` dono ka use socho.

title: Celsius To Fahrenheit
statement: Ek function `c_to_f(c)` likho jo Celsius temperature ko Fahrenheit mein badle (formula: `F = C * 9 / 5 + 32`) aur answer ko 1 decimal place tak `round` karke float return kare. Example: `c_to_f(100)` ka answer `212.0` hai.
solution:
def c_to_f(c):
    return round(c * 9 / 5 + 32, 1)
hint: Formula seedha lagao, phir `round(value, 1)` use karo.

title: First And Last Digit
statement: Ek function `first_last_sum(n)` likho jo integer `n` ke pehle aur aakhri digit ka sum return kare. Negative number ho to minus sign ignore karo. Single digit number mein wahi digit pehla bhi hai aur aakhri bhi. Example: `first_last_sum(1234)` ka answer `5` hai (1 + 4).
hint: `abs()` se sign hatao, phir number ko string bana kar index 0 aur -1 dekho.

title: Count Vowels
statement: Ek function `count_vowels(s)` likho jo string `s` mein vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) ki count return kare. Example: `count_vowels('Hello')` ka answer `2` hai.
hint: Pehle poori string ko `lower()` kar lo, phir har character check karo.

title: Name Initials
statement: Ek function `initials(name)` likho jo naam ke har word ka pehla letter capital karke uske baad ek dot laga kar ek string return kare. Words ke beech extra spaces ho sakte hain. Khaali naam par `''` return karo. Example: `initials('priya sharma')` ka answer `'P.S.'` hai.
hint: `split()` bina argument ke extra spaces khud sambhal leta hai.

title: Sentence Palindrome
statement: Ek function `is_palindrome(s)` likho jo `True` return kare agar string ulti padhne par bhi same ho, warna `False`. Check karte waqt spaces ignore karo aur uppercase/lowercase ka farak mat karo. Khaali string palindrome maani jaayegi. Example: `is_palindrome('never odd or even')` ka answer `True` hai.
hint: Pehle spaces hata kar sab lowercase karo, phir string ko uske reverse `[::-1]` se compare karo.

title: Mask Phone Number
statement: Ek function `mask_number(s)` likho jo string `s` ke aakhri 4 characters chhod kar baaki sab ko `*` se replace kare. Agar string ki length 4 ya usse kam hai to string waisi hi return karo. Example: `mask_number('9876543210')` ka answer `'******3210'` hai.
hint: String ko number se multiply karke repeat kar sakte ho, aur `s[-4:]` aakhri 4 characters deta hai.

title: Grade From Marks
statement: Ek function `grade(marks)` likho jo 0 se 100 ke marks ke hisaab se grade return kare: 90 ya usse upar `'S'`, 80-89 `'A'`, 70-79 `'B'`, 60-69 `'C'`, 50-59 `'D'`, 40-49 `'E'`, 40 se kam `'U'`. Agar marks 0 se kam ya 100 se zyada hain to `'Invalid'` return karo. Example: `grade(85)` ka answer `'A'` hai.
hint: Invalid case sabse pehle check karo, phir upar se neeche `if`/`elif` chain banao.

title: Triangle Type
statement: Ek function `triangle_type(a, b, c)` likho jo teen sides lekar triangle ka type return kare: `'equilateral'` (teeno barabar), `'isosceles'` (koi do barabar), `'scalene'` (sab alag). Agar koi side 0 ya negative hai, ya kisi do sides ka sum teesri side se bada nahi hai, to `'invalid'` return karo. Example: `triangle_type(3, 4, 5)` ka answer `'scalene'` hai.
hint: Pehle validity check karo (teeno pairs ka sum), type baad mein decide karo.

title: Count Divisors
statement: Ek function `count_divisors(n)` likho jo positive integer `n` ke kitne positive divisors hain, wo return kare. Example: `count_divisors(12)` ka answer `6` hai (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12).
hint: `range(1, n + 1)` par loop chala kar `n % d == 0` check karo.

title: Collatz Steps
statement: Ek function `collatz_steps(n)` likho jo positive integer `n` par yeh rule tab tak lagaye jab tak `n` 1 na ban jaaye: even ho to `n // 2`, odd ho to `3 * n + 1`. Kitne steps lage, wo return karo. Example: `collatz_steps(6)` ka answer `8` hai (6, 3, 10, 5, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1).
hint: `while n != 1` loop aur ek counter kaafi hai; `n = 1` par answer 0 hai.

title: Reverse A Number
statement: Ek function `reverse_number(n)` likho jo integer `n` ke digits ulte karke integer return kare. Sign waisa hi rehna chahiye aur leading zeros gayab ho jaayenge. Example: `reverse_number(-560)` ka answer `-65` hai.
solution:
def reverse_number(n):
    sign = -1 if n < 0 else 1
    n = abs(n)
    result = 0
    while n > 0:
        result = result * 10 + n % 10
        n = n // 10
    return sign * result
hint: `n % 10` aakhri digit deta hai aur `n // 10` use hata deta hai; sign alag se yaad rakho.

title: Prime Check
statement: Ek function `is_prime(n)` likho jo `True` return kare agar integer `n` prime hai, warna `False`. 1, 0 aur negative numbers prime nahi hote. Example: `is_prime(97)` ka answer `True` hai.
hint: Divisor dhoondhne ke liye sirf `sqrt(n)` tak check karna kaafi hai.

title: Number Triangle
statement: Ek function `triangle_rows(n)` likho jo strings ki list return kare jisme row `i` (1 se `n` tak) mein 1 se `i` tak ke numbers space se jude hon. `n` 0 ho to khaali list. Example: `triangle_rows(3)` ka answer `['1', '1 2', '1 2 3']` hai.
hint: Bahar ka loop rows ke liye, andar ka loop us row ke numbers ke liye; `' '.join()` se jodo.

title: Count Pairs With Sum
statement: Ek function `count_pairs(nums, target)` likho jo batata hai ki list mein kitne index pairs `(i, j)` hain jahan `i < j` aur `nums[i] + nums[j] == target`. Example: `count_pairs([1, 2, 3, 4, 3], 6)` ka answer `2` hai (2 + 4 aur 3 + 3).
hint: Andar wala loop `i + 1` se shuru karo taaki koi pair do baar na gina jaaye.

title: Times Table Grid
statement: Ek function `times_table(n)` likho jo `n x n` ki list of lists return kare jahan row `i` aur column `j` (dono 1 se shuru) par value `i * j` ho. `n` 0 ho to khaali list. Example: `times_table(2)` ka answer `[[1, 2], [2, 4]]` hai.
hint: Har row ke liye ek nayi list banao aur andar wale loop se bharo.

title: GCD By Euclid
statement: Ek function `my_gcd(a, b)` likho jo do non-negative integers ka GCD (greatest common divisor) return kare, bina `math` module ke. `my_gcd(0, 0)` ka answer `0` maano. Example: `my_gcd(12, 18)` ka answer `6` hai.
hint: Euclid ka idea: `gcd(a, b)` wahi hai jo `gcd(b, a % b)` hai, jab tak `b` zero na ho.

title: Discount Price
statement: Ek function `final_price(price, discount=10)` likho jo `discount` percent kam karke final price return kare, 2 decimal places tak `round` karke. Agar discount na diya jaaye to 10 percent maano. Example: `final_price(200)` ka answer `180.0` hai aur `final_price(200, 25)` ka `150.0`.
solution:
def final_price(price, discount=10):
    return round(price * (1 - discount / 100), 2)
hint: Default argument function signature mein hi likha jaata hai; percent ko 100 se divide karna mat bhoolna.

title: Second Largest
statement: Ek function `second_largest(nums)` likho jo list ka doosra sabse bada alag (distinct) number return kare. Agar aisa number exist nahi karta (khaali list, ek element, ya sab same) to `None` return karo. Example: `second_largest([4, 1, 7, 7, 3])` ka answer `4` hai.
hint: Duplicates hatane ke liye `set` kaam aayega; phir sort karke dekho.

title: Rotate Right
statement: Ek function `rotate_right(nums, k)` likho jo list ko `k` positions right rotate karke ek nayi list return kare (aakhri element aage aa jaata hai). `k` list ki length se bada bhi ho sakta hai. Example: `rotate_right([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 2)` ka answer `[4, 5, 1, 2, 3]` hai.
hint: `k % len(nums)` se extra rotations hatao, phir slicing se do tukde jodo.

title: Common Elements
statement: Ek function `common_sorted(a, b)` likho jo dono lists mein common elements ki sorted list return kare, bina duplicates ke. Example: `common_sorted([3, 1, 4, 1, 5], [5, 9, 1])` ka answer `[1, 5]` hai.
solution:
def common_sorted(a, b):
    return sorted(set(a) & set(b))
hint: Sets ka intersection operator `&` yahan kaam aayega.

title: Unique Word Count
statement: Ek function `unique_word_count(sentence)` likho jo sentence mein kitne alag words hain, wo return kare. Words space se alag hain, case-insensitive compare karo, aur har word ke shuru/aakhir se `. , ! ?` hata do. Jo word in characters ko hatane ke baad khaali ho jaaye use mat gino. Example: `unique_word_count('The cat and the hat.')` ka answer `4` hai.
hint: `strip('.,!?')` aur `lower()` ke baad words ko ek `set` mein daalo.

title: Character Frequency
statement: Ek function `char_freq(s)` likho jo ek dictionary return kare jisme har character (space chhod kar) kitni baar aaya, wo ho. Keys usi order mein hon jis order mein character pehli baar aaya. Uppercase aur lowercase alag gine jaayenge. Example: `char_freq('banana')` ka answer `{'b': 1, 'a': 3, 'n': 2}` hai.
hint: `dict.get(key, 0) + 1` se counting aasaan ho jaati hai.

title: Group Keys By Value
statement: Ek function `group_by_value(d)` likho jo dictionary `d` ko ulta kare: naye dictionary mein har value ek key bane aur uski value un sab keys ki list ho jinki value wahi thi (original order mein). Example: `group_by_value({'a': 1, 'b': 2, 'c': 1})` ka answer `{1: ['a', 'c'], 2: ['b']}` hai.
hint: Agar value pehli baar mili hai to uske liye khaali list banao, phir key append karo.

title: Top Student
statement: Ek function `top_student(marks)` likho jo dictionary (naam -> marks) mein sabse zyada marks wale student ka naam return kare. Tie ho to alphabetically pehla naam return karo. Dictionary khaali ho to `None`. Example: `top_student({'Asha': 82, 'Ravi': 91})` ka answer `'Ravi'` hai.
hint: Ab tak ka best naam yaad rakho; tie par naamon ko `<` se compare karo.

title: Even Squares
statement: Ek function `even_squares(nums)` likho jo list comprehension se sirf even numbers ke squares ki list return kare, original order mein. Example: `even_squares([1, 2, 3, 4])` ka answer `[4, 16]` hai.
solution:
def even_squares(nums):
    return [x * x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0]
hint: Comprehension ka format: `[expression for x in list if condition]`.

title: Transpose Matrix
statement: Ek function `transpose(matrix)` likho jo list of lists (sab rows ki length same) ka transpose return kare: rows columns ban jaati hain. Khaali matrix par `[]` return karo. Example: `transpose([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])` ka answer `[[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6]]` hai.
hint: Nested comprehension: bahar column index `j` par loop, andar har row se `row[j]` lo.

title: Flatten Nested List
statement: Ek recursive function `flatten(nested)` likho jo kisi bhi depth tak nested list ko ek seedhi (flat) list mein badal de, order same rakhte hue. Example: `flatten([1, [2, [3, 4]], 5])` ka answer `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` hai.
hint: Har item ke liye `isinstance(item, list)` check karo; list ho to usi function ko dobara call karo.

title: Digital Root
statement: Ek recursive function `digital_root(n)` likho jo non-negative integer `n` ke digits ka sum tab tak nikaale jab tak ek single digit na bache, aur wo digit return kare. Example: `digital_root(9875)` ka answer `2` hai (9875 -> 29 -> 11 -> 2).
hint: Base case: `n < 10` ho to wahi answer hai; warna digits ka sum nikaal kar function dobara call karo.

title: Rectangle Class
statement: Ek class `Rectangle` banao jiska constructor `Rectangle(width, height)` ho aur teen methods hon: `area()` jo area return kare, `perimeter()` jo perimeter return kare, aur `is_square()` jo `True` return kare agar width aur height barabar hon. Example: `Rectangle(3, 4).area()` ka answer `12` hai.
hint: `__init__` mein values ko `self.width` aur `self.height` mein save karo, phir methods mein unhe use karo.

title: Run Length Compress
statement: Ek function `compress(s)` likho jo string ko compress kare: lagataar aane wale same characters ke group ko character aur uske count se replace karo. Agar count 1 hai to sirf character likho. Uppercase aur lowercase alag characters hain. Example: `compress('aaabccdddd')` ka answer `'a3bc2d4'` hai.
hint: Current character aur uska count yaad rakho; character badalte hi pichla group result mein likh do, aur loop ke baad aakhri group mat bhoolna.

title: Expense Category Totals
statement: Ek function `category_totals(entries)` likho jo strings ki list le, jahan har entry ka format `'date|category|amount'` hai. Har category ka total amount nikaalo aur ek dictionary return karo jiski keys alphabetical order mein hon. Category ke aas-paas ke spaces hatao aur use lowercase mein badlo. Amount float hai (negative bhi ho sakta hai, jaise refund). Jis entry mein `|` se split karne par exactly 3 parts na hon use ignore karo. Har total 2 decimal places tak round karo. Example: `category_totals(['d1|food|120.5', 'd2|Food|79.5', 'oops'])` ka answer `{'food': 200.0}` hai.
hint: Pehle sab totals ek normal dict mein jodo, aur aakhir mein `sorted(keys)` ke order mein naya dict banao.

title: Spiral Order
statement: Ek function `spiral_order(matrix)` likho jo ek rectangular matrix (list of lists) ke saare elements spiral order mein list ke roop mein return kare: pehle top row left se right, phir right column upar se neeche, phir bottom row right se left, phir left column neeche se upar, aur yahi andar ki taraf repeat. Khaali matrix par `[]`. Example: `spiral_order([[1, 2], [3, 4]])` ka answer `[1, 2, 4, 3]` hai.
hint: Chaar boundaries (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`) rakho aur har side padhne ke baad use andar khiskao; neeche aur left wali side se pehle check karo ki boundary cross to nahi hui.

title: Merge Store Inventories
statement: Do dukaanon ka stock dictionaries mein hai: `{item: {'qty': quantity, 'price': price}}`. Ek function `merge_inventories(store_a, store_b)` likho jo ek naya dictionary return kare jisme har item ki total `qty` (dono dukaanon ka sum) ho aur `price` un dukaanon ka minimum price ho jahan us item ki `qty` 0 se zyada hai. Jis item ki kahin bhi `qty` 0 se zyada nahi hai use result mein mat rakho. Result ki keys alphabetical order mein hon, aur input dictionaries change nahi honi chahiye. Example: `merge_inventories({'pen': {'qty': 10, 'price': 5}}, {'pen': {'qty': 4, 'price': 4}})` ka answer `{'pen': {'qty': 14, 'price': 4}}` hai.
hint: Input ki inner dicts ko seedha result mein mat daalo, nayi dict banao; warna original data badal jaayega.

title: Shift Cipher
statement: Ek function `caesar_shift(text, k)` likho jo har English letter ko alphabet mein `k` positions aage khiskaye (z ke baad wapas a). Uppercase letter uppercase rahe, lowercase lowercase. Letters ke alawa sab characters waise hi rahein. `k` negative ya 26 se bada bhi ho sakta hai. Example: `caesar_shift('xyz', 2)` ka answer `'zab'` hai.
hint: `ord()` se letter ko 0-25 position mein badlo, `% 26` lagao, phir `chr()` se wapas letter banao.

title: Words By Length
statement: Ek function `length_buckets(sentence)` likho jo sentence ke words ko unki length ke hisaab se group kare. Words whitespace se alag hain; har word ke shuru/aakhir se `. , ! ? ; :` hatao aur lowercase karo; jo word khaali ho jaaye use chhod do. Return ek dictionary karo jiski keys lengths hon (badhte order mein) aur value us length ke alag-alag words ki sorted list ho. Example: `length_buckets('a bb a ccc bb')` ka answer `{1: ['a'], 2: ['bb'], 3: ['ccc']}` hai.
hint: Pehle har length ke liye ek `set` mein words jamaa karo, aakhir mein keys aur values dono sort karo.

tests.call: length_buckets('The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.')

title: Longest Step Streak
statement: Ek fitness app har din ke steps ek list `steps` mein rakhta hai. Ek function `longest_streak(steps, target)` likho jo sabse lambi lagataar streak dhoondhe jisme har din steps `target` ke barabar ya zyada the, aur tuple `(length, start_index)` return kare. Barabar length ki do streaks hon to pehle wali lo. Koi bhi aisa din na ho to `(0, -1)` return karo. Example: `longest_streak([4000, 8000, 9000, 10000, 3000], 8000)` ka answer `(3, 1)` hai.
hint: Current streak ki length aur shuru ka index track karo; best ko sirf tab update karo jab current strictly bada ho.

title: Pass In Every Subject
statement: Ek function `top_passers(csv_text)` likho jo ek multi-line string le. Pehli line header hai, jaise `name,maths,stats,python` (subjects ki ginti kuch bhi ho sakti hai). Baaki har line mein ek student ka naam aur har subject ke integer marks comma se alag hain. Har value ke aas-paas ke spaces hatao aur khaali lines ignore karo. Un students ke naam ki list return karo jinke har subject mein marks 40 ya usse zyada hain, total marks ke ghatte order mein; total barabar ho to naam ke alphabetical order mein. Example: `top_passers('name,a,b\nRavi,50,60\nSita,30,90')` ka answer `['Ravi']` hai.
hint: Har line ko `split(',')` karke marks ko `int` mein badlo; sort ke liye `(-total, name)` jaisa tuple key kaam aata hai.

title: Password Checker
statement: Ek function `password_issues(pw)` likho jo password mein jo-jo rules fail hue unke naam ki list return kare, isi fixed order mein: `'length'` (8 se kam characters), `'upper'` (koi uppercase letter nahi), `'lower'` (koi lowercase letter nahi), `'digit'` (koi digit nahi), `'special'` (`!@#$%&*` mein se koi character nahi), `'space'` (password mein space hai). Sab rules pass hon to khaali list return karo. Example: `password_issues('abc')` ka answer `['length', 'upper', 'digit', 'special']` hai.
hint: Har rule ke liye alag `if` likho (elif nahi), aur `any()` se check karo ki koi character condition poori karta hai ya nahi.

title: Split The Bill
statement: Doston ka ek group kharcha barabar baant-ta hai. Ek function `settle_balances(members, expenses)` likho jahan `members` naamon ki list hai aur `expenses` tuples `(payer, amount)` ki list hai. Har member ka share = total kharcha / members ki ginti. Har member ke liye `paid - share` nikaalo (positive matlab use paise wapas milne hain), 2 decimal places tak round karo, aur naam ke alphabetical order mein dictionary return karo. Jisne kuch nahi diya uska paid 0 hai. `members` khaali ho to `{}` return karo. Example: `settle_balances(['A', 'B'], [('A', 100)])` ka answer `{'A': 50.0, 'B': -50.0}` hai.
hint: Pehle har member ka total paid ek dict mein jodo, phir share ek baar nikaal kar sab par lagao.

title: Nested Path Lookup
statement: Ek function `get_path(data, path)` likho jo nested dicts aur lists ke andar dot se alag path follow karke value return kare. Path ka har part: agar current value dict hai to wo key honi chahiye; agar list hai to part ek non-negative integer index (sirf digits) hona chahiye jo range mein ho. Kisi bhi step par yeh na ho paaye (key missing, index galat, ya dict/list ke alawa kuch aur mile) to `None` return karo. Khaali path par poora `data` return karo. Example: `get_path({'a': {'b': [10, 20]}}, 'a.b.1')` ka answer `20` hai.
hint: Har step par pehle type check karo (`isinstance`); list ke liye `part.isdigit()` aur range dono dekho.

title: League Points Table
statement: Ek function `league_table(results)` likho jo match results ki list le, har result ka format `'TeamA goalsA-goalsB TeamB'` hai (team names ek word ke, beech mein extra spaces ho sakte hain). Jeet par 3 points, draw par 1, haar par 0. Har team ka goal difference (kiye gaye goals minus khaaye gaye) bhi nikaalo. Tuples `(team, points, goal_difference)` ki list return karo, points ke ghatte order mein; points barabar hon to goal difference ke ghatte order mein; woh bhi barabar ho to naam ke alphabetical order mein. Example: `league_table(['A 1-1 B'])` ka answer `[('A', 1, 0), ('B', 1, 0)]` hai.
hint: Points aur goal difference ke liye do dicts rakho; aakhir mein `sort(key=lambda row: (-points, -diff, name))` jaisa key use karo.
